summary: Intermittent 429s during high-cardinality short-lived streaming sessions (Dedicated pool)
description: Issue summary: BrightLearn reports intermittent 429 throttles impacting their dedicated pool during recurring overnight jobs that open many short-lived streaming sessions. Impact: ~10-25% of requests for a customer endpoint receive 429s for ~1-3 minute windows, causing ingestion backfills to fail and downstream customer jobs to retry heavily. Environment: Dedicated pool (customer-dedicated-3), production, us-east. Observed behaviour: bursts of very short sessions (~1-3 tokens/session, lasting <5s) correlate with tenant-level 429s; aggregated tenant token accounting shows rapid depletion despite low per-session token counts. Expected behaviour: short sessions should be aggregated so tenant quotas are not exhausted by cardinality of connections alone.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer runs a fan-out ingest: N workers concurrently open SSE streaming sessions to the Redwood streaming endpoint (N=1,200).
2) Each session sends very small payloads (1-3 tokens) then closes after ~2-4s.
3) Observe token/quota accounting and responses from the API; repeat at 3-4 minute intervals.
4) Observe intermittent 429s appear within the same tenant window correlated to the fanout start times.
investigation_notes: - Support reproduced in staging with a synthetic fanout harness (1,000 concurrent short sessions) and saw tenant 429s within 60-90s.
- Rate-limiter logs show many distinct connection IDs mapped to per-route buckets; aggregated tenant token counter increased quickly and hit burst cap.
- Serving runtime traces show each stream created a separate accounting entry; prefix/KV caching not effective because sessions are ephemeral and payloads are tiny.
- No 5xx errors observed; error class is 429 with response code path 'quota_exceeded.tenant_burst'.
- Heap and CPU on dedicated pool nodes are normal; not a noisy-neighbor or GPU shortage.
root_cause: High cardinality of short-lived streaming sessions caused the per-connection accounting to create many token-buckets and caused tenant-level burst accounting to be consumed before aggregation could amortize cost. The rate-limiter treats each short stream as a separate burst contributor which, at large fanout, depleted the tenant burst window.
fix_plan: Short-term mitigation: increase tenant burst window and per-connection aggregation timeout for this dedicated pool (config change) to allow short sessions to collapse into aggregate accounting.

Medium-term: implement server-side short-session aggregation (coalesce ephemeral streams under the same tenant key within a 10s window) and update guidance for dedicated customers doing high-cardinality fanouts.
Long-term: expose a dedicated-pool flag to opt into 'short_session_aggregation' and document recommended client-side best practices (connection reuse, multiplexing).
resolution: 2026-03-11 04:20 UTC - Applied temporary config: tenant burst window increased from 60s to 180s for customer-dedicated-3. Observed immediate reduction in 429s for reproduction harness.
2026-03-11 11:00 UTC - Enabled connection-reuse recommendation with BrightLearn engineers; they rolled a patch to multiplex streams into persistent connections which reduced cardinality by ~6x.
Follow-up: engineering ticket INT-4512 created to implement server-side aggregation (target sprint: 2026-03-29).
